transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-12-08
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~62 minutes
Attendees: Ethan Park, Sofia Ramos (Redwood); Priya Nair, Marco DeLuca, Janelle Ortiz, Anil Rao (Ivybridge)

Auto-summary (quick):
Ivybridge is scoping a 4-6 week POC to validate private connectivity and data residency constraints for a pilot inference workload. Main decision points: VPC peering vs PrivateLink, region locking to us-west-2, egress controls to prevent cross-region replication, and target SLOs for latency (p99) and throughput. Action items: Redwood to provide bench scripts and runbook; Ivybridge to provide network details and compliance constraints.

Topics:
- Workload sizing: concurrent sessions, typical tokens, bursts
- Benchmark targets: rps, tokens/sec, latency percentiles
- Networking options: VPC peering vs AWS PrivateLink vs NAT egress control
- Data residency & region lockdown
- POC timeline and success criteria

Transcript body:
[00:00] Ethan Park: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, we'll give a quick agenda, then deep dive into the network topologies and the benchmarks. I think we have about an hour, correct?
[00:08] Priya Nair: Yes, thanks Ethan. Appreciate you fitting us in. We want to make sure this POC actually proves we can run inference within our region with no egress, and keep under our cost targets.
[00:18] Sofia Ramos: Hi all, Sofia here, I'm the sales engineer on this, I'll run the perf stuff and map the routing options. Quick clarifier — is the primary requirement strict region-locking or is cross-region allowed for backups?
[00:28] Janelle Ortiz: Strict for inference path. Backups maybe to a secondary region but must be encrypted and governed. No egress to public internet for inference requests or payloads.
[00:37] Marco DeLuca: For context, our infra is in us-west-2. We use Transit Gateway right now for some multi-account peering, but we don't want a public endpoint. Ideally a privatelink endpoint or peering, depending on cost and scale.
[00:48] Ethan Park: Great. We'll talk through trade-offs. High-level: VPC peering gives you low-latency path but requires route table management and transitive routing might be limited; PrivateLink puts a network interface in your subnet — easier from an isolation standpoint and you can enforce endpoint policies, but the throughput characteristics and per-GB egress pricing differ.
[01:05] Anil Rao: Curious on throughput — if we run 100 concurrent sessions with occasional 4k-token generations, what should we expect p99 latency to look like?
[01:13] Sofia Ramos: Good question. Depends on model size and batch settings. For a 13B-ish model with quantized path on T4 equivalent, from our hosted environment you'd see tail latency p99 in the ~700-900ms range for single-turn 4k tokens if it's cold, but with KV cache and batching it can be down to 200-400ms. For peering vs privatelink we typically see <10% variance in latency but throughput caps and per-GB charges differ.
[01:34] Marco DeLuca: The per-GB charge is a sticking point for us, we have a prediction of 5 TB/month egress if not managed.
[01:41] Ethan Park: Right, we need to plan for caching and prefix reuse to reduce tokens. Also our Redwood Optimize recommendations will suggest batching windows and shared KV caches for repeated prompts.
[01:50] Priya Nair: Let's outline success criteria now so we can be clear. I'll suggest: (1) p99 latency < 1.2s for our 90% of workloads, (2) sustained 100 concurrent sessions at peaks with <5% error rate, (3) all inference traffic contained in us-west-2 with egress audit logs, and (4) cost per 1k tokens under $0.30 for the pilot. Thoughts?
[02:10] Janelle Ortiz: From security, add: SOC2 audit entries for every inference call, KMS envelope encryption for models and payloads, and 90-day access logs retained.
[02:20] Ethan Park: Those are reasonable. For logs we can stream audit logs to your account via PrivateLink/peering flow logs or syslog — we'll show options.
[02:28] Sofia Ramos: On the benchmark approach: we'll run two tracks — a functional validation track that focuses on isolation (confirm no cross-region), and a perf track with a scripted load that simulates 100 concurrent sessions, 4k token bursts mixed with 128-token quick queries at a 70/30 split. We'll collect p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec and token-cost metrics.
[02:50] Anil Rao: Can you share the perf script so we can vet it? We have internal traces to match the distribution.
[02:54] Sofia Ramos: Yes, action — I'll attach the script to the sheet. We'll use a runner that supports KV warmup so we can show cold vs warmed runs.
[03:02] Marco DeLuca: On the network side I want to map what needs to be opened. If we go with VPC peering we need route entries between Redwood subnets and our processing subnets. If PrivateLink, we need to accept the endpoint service and allow ENI creation — and then we'll apply SG rules to lock down. Which approach offers better egress control?
[03:21] Ethan Park: Both can be controlled. PrivateLink can be easier for strict isolation because the endpoint is in your VPC and traffic never transits the public internet; you can also apply endpoint policies and block certain APIs. Peering gives you full L3 reach but requires careful route control to prevent accidental cross-account routes. For strict egress audit, PrivateLink + Flow Logs to your account + endpoint policies is a common enterprise pattern.
[03:42] Janelle Ortiz: We're also considering using an egress proxy in our account to restrict destinations. Is that compatible with Redwood's run-time?
[03:49] Sofia Ramos: Yes, you can front the requests through a NAT/egress proxy; the runner will still see the same IP path, but note that adding a proxy adds a hair of latency and complicates certificate rotation. We'll measure that in the perf runs.
[04:00] Priya Nair: Timelines — we want a 4-week POC: week 0-1 setup and connectivity, week 2 perf baselines, week 3 tuning and re-runs with KV warmed, week 4 security verification and sign-off. Are those realistic?
[04:13] Ethan Park: Yes, and we usually do a 2-week prep to get accounts and IAM in place. So calendar-wise, if we start next week we can complete by mid-January. However, third-party approvals from your InfoSec might push it out a bit.
[04:25] Marco DeLuca: We'll need a template IAM role and least-privilege policy for Redwood read-only metrics access — can't have broad S3 access.
[04:32] Ethan Park: We'll provide an IAM trust role with specific CloudWatch and VPC Flow Log read/write permissions. We'll also provide a runbook for trust boundaries.
[04:40] Anil Rao: A couple of technical clarifications — does Redwood's runtime require outbound egress to other regions for model fetches or telemetry? We need to ensure no model artifacts leave us-west-2.
[04:50] Sofia Ramos: For Private deployments, model bits are stored in your region. For our hosted/dedicated offering, we can pin model artifacts to a regional bucket. Telemetry by default streams to Redwood control plane but for Private deployment we can configure telemetry to push to your account. For the hosted POC we'll demonstrate via a VPC-hosted endpoint plus a restricted telemetry sink so nothing leaves the region unencrypted.
[05:10] Janelle Ortiz: We want KMS keys we control — CMKs in our account. Can Redwood integrate with external key holders?
[05:17] Ethan Park: Yes, we support customer-managed keys (CMKs) and HSM integrations for Private deployments. For the POC we'll use your CMK and show end-to-end encryption of model payloads and logs.
[05:26] Priya Nair: Bench numbers — can you put some expected ranges in the doc? For executive-level expectation setting.
[05:32] Sofia Ramos: Sure, preliminary numbers (subject to hardware):
- Baseline single-thread token throughput: ~120-200 tokens/sec on mid-range GPU for a 13B model
- Batched throughput (100 concurrent with 8 token batching): effective tokens/sec scales to ~3-6k tokens/sec depending on sequence lengths
- Latency p99: cold 800ms-1.5s; warmed/cache 180ms-600ms for single-turns
- Error rate target: <1% for stable model backends
These are ballpark — we'll run the scripts to get precise numbers for your config.
[06:05] Marco DeLuca: For the POC, we plan to run both a synthetic workload and a replay of 48 hours of production traces (anonymized). Can your bench runner replay that?
[06:12] Sofia Ramos: Yes, we can replay traces; we recommend sampling and chunking to focus on representative prompts. We'll also show token distribution and cache hit rates.
[06:20] Ethan Park: Another point — we should instrument canary routes so if a model variant fails we'll fallback to a smaller model in the same region. That reduces risk of global egress when larger models OOM.
[06:30] Priya Nair: Good. On cost — if privatelink charges push us over budget, we might prefer peering with tight route control. Can you model cost per TB for both options?
[06:39] Ethan Park: Yes, we'll model network charges plus per-token inference cost and show TCO per million tokens. We'll include sensitivity analysis for 1TB, 5TB, 10TB monthly volumes.
[06:50] Janelle Ortiz: Compliance review — we need an audit pack that includes SOC2 controls, diagrams of data flows, and proof of encryption-in-transit and at-rest. Can Redwood attach that to the POC deliverables?
[06:59] Ethan Park: Absolutely. We'll attach security docs and our SOC2 attestation, and provide the flow diagrams for the chosen topology.
[07:05] Anil Rao: Slight nit — you mentioned KV cache earlier; how do we ensure consistency when we have autoscaling? Will caches be shared or per-instance?
[07:12] Sofia Ramos: Our runtime supports shared KV caches within a pool; for Dedicated pools we can pin a global cache service so warmups propagate. If you're using autoscaling across accounts, we can set sticky routing to keep KV locality. We'll show config options in the runbook.
[07:26] Priya Nair: Anything else we should call out?
[07:30] Marco DeLuca: One more — can we run the perf test with our egress proxy in place? I want to see the added latency.
[07:35] Sofia Ramos: Yes, we'll run three passes: direct peering, PrivateLink, and PrivateLink + egress proxy.
[07:41] Ethan Park: Ok let's recap and assign owners. We'll send the benchmark spreadsheet and scripts, you'll share the network details and compliance constraints, and we'll schedule the bench runs.
[07:52] Priya Nair: Sounds good. Appreciate the clarity — this helps our procurement discussions too.
[07:58] Ethan Park: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the runbook and cost model by Friday.

Meeting end.
crm_notes: POC focused on strict region-locking and egress audit. Priority: network isolation first, perf second. Customer is cost-sensitive re: egress TB pricing. InfoSec will need SOC2 evidence, CMK support, and 90-day logs.
